name: auto-editor
role: CLI that finds silent or static spans and exports the cuts as a timeline or rendered rough cut
summary: CLI that cuts silent (`--edit audio`) or low-motion (`--edit motion`) spans from video or audio and renders the result or exports a timeline (v1 chunks, v3 JSON, Premiere XML, others). It writes the rough cut of a recorded take; it does not detect shots or edit timelines by hand.
use_when: Cut dead air from recorded narration or a screen-capture take before pacing review
Export the cut points as a timeline for assembly with FFmpeg, instead of its own re-encode
avoid_when: Finding shot cuts in footage: pyscenedetect
Editing a timeline you write by hand: opentimelineio or mlt-melt

install.macos: python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install auto-editor==29.3.1

notes: 2026-11-27: the lead said Homebrew 31.10.0; the PyPI launcher stops at 29.3.1 and downloads its native binary from GitHub on first run. Export names are v1, v3, premiere (not json); the -o extension does not choose the format.

assessment.rationale: Lead: repository pushed 2026-11-25 (not rechecked); Homebrew 31.10.0 is newer than PyPI 29.3.1, which was the tested version. Nothing catalogued cuts silence: pyscenedetect finds visual cuts, opentimelineio and mlt-melt edit timelines you write. Major versions change the CLI, so pin the version.

evidence.result: 7 checks pass, repeat processes identical: on a generated 2 s tone, 3 s silence, 2 s tone clip, v1 chunks, v3 clips and Premiere XML cut exactly frames 60-150 (2.0-5.0 s), FFmpeg silencedetect agrees, rendered cut is 4.0 s. Python 3.12.2.
evidence.scope: Audio silence cuts on synthetic tones, threshold 0.04, margin 0; v1, v3, premiere exports; not speech, motion edit, 31.x, other exports or OTIO import; macOS arm64.
